contamination_check._why: Once the retracted meta-analysis turned out to rest on a retracted study and a study measuring self-efficacy, the obvious question was whether the surviving one rests on the same material. Asking it was necessary; assuming the answer either way would have been the error we recorded this morning.
contamination_check.checked: 2026-08-29. The article's reference PDF was searched for the five studies Ingebrigtsen & Lukic identify as the worst in Wang & Fan.
contamination_check.result: NOT FOUND: Chan et al. (2024b, the retracted one), Ji et al. (2023, the g = 4.009 clustering error), Huang et al. (2024, the self-efficacy study), Hsu (2024, the 80-vs-20-hours confound), Almohesh (2024). FOUND: a Chen & Chang (2024) — 'Effectiveness of AI-assisted game-based learning on science learning outcomes, intrinsic motivation, cognitive load, and learning behavior', Education and Information Technologies — which may or may not be the Chen and Chang paper Ingebrigtsen & Lukic say appears four times in Wang & Fan under two different education levels. We cannot tell from the citation and must not guess.
contamination_check.STRENGTH_OF_THIS_FINDING: WEAK. It is a machine read of a reference PDF by a summarising model, not our own eyes on the list, and such a read can truncate. A 'not found' from it is not proof of absence. Before anything is printed either way, somebody reads the reference list directly.
contamination_check.what_it_means_if_it_holds: That the surviving meta-analysis is NOT built on the same bad material, and the piece must say so. The temptation to let a retraction next door discredit a neighbouring paper is exactly the reasoning we recorded as CHAIN_BETWEEN_DOCUMENTS_ASSUMED.
contamination_check.what_still_stands_against_it_regardless: Its own account of its own methods. It reports the funnel plot as symmetric on visual inspection, and uses the classic fail-safe N — a method Borenstein (2019, pp. 180-181) and Van Aert, Wicherts & Van Assen (2019) advise against for assessing publication bias. That is a criticism of a stated method, sourced to methodologists, and it stands without reference to what happened to Wang & Fan. IT IS OURS, not anybody else's finding, and the counterexample hunter should be pointed at it.
contamination_check.second_attempt_2026_08_29:
Went back to transcribe the reference list rather than ask a model to search it. The A-D range came back verbatim and complete-looking: no Almohesh (2024), and no Chan, Lo & Wong essay-writing paper — the retracted one. Chan, C.K.Y. & Lee and Chan, C.K.Y. & Zhou are present and are a different Chan (Cecilia Chan, HKU). Chen, C.H. & Chang, C.L. (2024), 'Effectiveness of AI-assisted game-based learning...', Education and Information Technologies, IS present; whether it is the Chen and Chang paper Ingebrigtsen & Lukic say appears four times in Wang & Fan cannot be told from the citation.

The E-L pass came back PARAPHRASED rather than transcribed, and a targeted H-J pass returned 'full reference not included' — the fetch is truncating the PDF. So Ji (2023), Huang (2024) and Hsu (2024) CANNOT BE SETTLED this way.
contamination_check.STATUS: TWO OF FIVE confidently absent (Almohesh, Chan et al. 2024b). THREE UNSETTLED (Ji, Huang, Hsu).
contamination_check.AND_IT_IS_THE_WRONG_TEST_ANYWAY: A reference list mixes included studies with cited works — Cohen (1992), Anderson & Krathwohl (2001) and Biggs et al. (2022) are all in it. The question 'which 35 studies were included' is answered by the study-characteristics table, not the bibliography. We were about to settle a question with an instrument that cannot answer it.
contamination_check.DECISION:
DOWNGRADED from blocking to optional, and the piece is rewritten not to need it. We do not have to certify Wu et al. as clean. What is true, checkable and sufficient is what the paper says about ITSELF: its publication-bias assessment is a funnel plot judged by eye plus Begg's test and a classic fail-safe N — a method Borenstein (2019) and Van Aert et al. (2019) advise against for this purpose — and it does not state whether its post-tests were taken with ChatGPT available, and reports no delayed or retention measure. That stands on the paper's own account and needs no adjudication of what it included.

One fact worth keeping: Wu et al. DOES cite Deng et al. (2025), the meta-analysis Weidlich and colleagues audited. Confirmed in the verbatim A-D pass.

sources.authors: Magnus Ingebrigtsen (Department of Psychology, UiT The Arctic University of Norway) and Marko Lukic (Centre for Faculty Development (HelPed), UiT). Competing interests: none declared. They thank Torstein Låg of the UiT University Library for advice on assessing bias in meta-analysis.

what_it_actually_says.the_corrected_effect: 'the funnel plot for learning performance indicates that the pooled effect size was approximately 0.5, and not 0.867.' READ OFF WANG AND FAN'S OWN FUNNEL PLOT — not a recomputation, and NOT a forest plot. Plagiarism Today said forest plot. It is wrong.
what_it_actually_says.the_retracted_study: Chan, Lo & Wong (2024b), '[RETRACTED] Generative AI and Essay Writing: Impacts of Automated Feedback on Revision Performance and Engagement', rEFLections 31(3) 1249-1284. It had the LOWEST standard error in the whole meta-analysis, SE = 0.066, carrying about 19% of the total weight, and it had been officially retracted TWO MONTHS BEFORE Wang and Fan's paper was published. Ingebrigtsen and Lukic further note the same study appears in two other journals with acceptance dates of October 2024 and December 2024.
what_it_actually_says.the_second_heaviest_study: Huang, Liu & Dong (2024), SE = 0.092, roughly 10% of total weight — AND IT DID NOT MEASURE LEARNING PERFORMANCE. Its outcomes were self-efficacy and technology acceptance. So two studies contributing nearly 30% of the weight, one retracted and one measuring a different construct entirely.
what_it_actually_says.how_many_studies: Table 3 lists only 41 unique entries for learning performance while the analysis reports k = 44. Two entries for Bašić et al. (2023a, 2023b) with a participant count matching only one of the cited papers. Chen and Chang (2024), who studied 7th graders, appear FOUR times — two entries labelled 'college' and two 'secondary'. One entry is itself a meta-analysis, contradicting the authors' own inclusion criteria.
what_it_actually_says.the_clustering_error: Ji et al. (2023) divided 36 students into groups of five to six, each group receiving a single shared grade. Wang and Fan treated it as though each student had an individual score. Ignoring the clustering artificially reduces variance and inflates the effect, which was entered as g = 4.009.
what_it_actually_says.sample_size_discrepancies: Chan et al. (2024b) reported 918 participants, but its t-test degrees of freedom (192) indicate only 194 analysed. Almohesh (2024) reports 250 participants in the abstract and 150 in the results.
what_it_actually_says.the_confounding: Many included studies are quasi-experimental and do not control time-on-task. In Hsu (2024) the ChatGPT group practised medical terminology for about 80 hours against the control group's 20.
what_it_actually_says.the_generalising_claim: Effect sizes above 1 are rare in educational research (citing Kraft 2023), yet appear in ABOUT 36% of Wang and Fan's included studies. Ingebrigtsen and Lukic call this 'systemic overestimation'. This is the one place they generalise beyond the single paper.
what_it_actually_says.on_publication_bias_method: Wang and Fan relied on Fail-safe N, which Ingebrigtsen and Lukic note experts strongly advise against for this purpose, citing Borenstein (2019, pp. 180-181) and Van Aert, Wicherts & Van Assen (2019). They also say Wang and Fan declared their funnel plots symmetric despite visual evidence otherwise, and that standard tests for funnel asymmetry would 'clearly' have shown asymmetry.
what_it_actually_says.the_correspondence: They contacted the authors directly under Springer Nature's policy and asked for the dataset and a forest plot, which the paper did not contain. WANG AND FAN REPLIED PROMPTLY, attributing several discrepancies to 'a formatting error during the typesetting process'. They did not supply a complete dataset. Their data availability statement read: 'No datasets were generated or analysed during the current study.' Problems remained unresolved after two weeks of correspondence, at which point the critics asked the editors to consider retraction.

corrections_to_our_record: We had 'forest plot'. It is the FUNNEL plot. That came from Plagiarism Today and was wrong.

We had, from the retraction notice, 'the authors have not responded to correspondence'. That is true of the journal's correspondence about the retraction in 2026. It is NOT true of the critics' approach in June 2025, which Wang and Fan answered promptly. Printing the first without the second would have been unfair to them.

We had a vague 'improper weighting'. The actual finding is sharper and more damaging: the two heaviest studies, together nearly 30% of the weight, were one retracted paper and one that measured self-efficacy rather than learning.

sources.the_precise_criticism: Not 'it is only a correlation' — the author says that himself. The point is that all three constructs are self-reported in one instrument, and the three correlations are uniformly strong: 0.68, 0.72, 0.75. That uniformity is the signature of common-method variance rather than three separately established relationships. Note also that the critical-thinking items are DERIVED from the Halpern assessment rather than being the Halpern assessment administered as a test; the piece must say 'items drawn from' and not imply a test was sat.

what_it_actually_says.THE_ANSWER_TO_THE_QUESTION_THAT_MATTERED: Accuracy was measured WITH THE AI AVAILABLE. Participants worked seven open-ended CRT items with an assistant embedded in the survey and 'retained full autonomy over whether to follow its suggestions'. This is a DEFERENCE measure, not an after-the-tool-is-gone measure. Our own file had it filed under 'measures unassisted performance', and that was wrong. It is not a flaw in the study — assisted performance is exactly the right measure for deference — it was a flaw in our filing.
what_it_actually_says.design: Three preregistered experiments plus a preregistered trial-level synthesis. Seven open-ended CRT items adapted from Manfredi & Nave (2022). AI was ChatGPT (GPT-4o) embedded in each trial, returning either the correct deliberative answer (AI-Accurate) or a confidently presented intuitive error (AI-Faulty) with a short rationale, randomised at item level via hidden seed prompts. Data collected in person (private cubicles, standardised hardware) and online (desktop/laptop only). Penn IRB #858904. Materials, preregistrations and codebooks on OSF. Funded by the Wharton Behavioral Lab.
what_it_actually_says.study_1: N = 359, in person. Brain-Only n = 121, AI-Assisted n = 238 (oversampled 2:1). Plus an ancillary online sample of 81, excluded from Study 1 results but included in the synthesis. Chat used on 54.4% of AI-Accurate and 52.8% of AI-Faulty trials. CONDITIONAL ON USING IT: followed the AI on 92.7% of accurate trials and 79.8% of FAULTY trials — overriding a wrong answer only one time in five. Accuracy: Brain-Only 45.8% [42.5, 49.2]; AI-Accurate 71.0% [67.9, 74.1]; AI-Faulty 31.5% [28.3, 34.6]. Accurate vs faulty OR = 0.07 [0.05, 0.11] — about 14 times lower odds of being right. Cohen's h = 0.81 [0.72, 0.91].
what_it_actually_says.the_confidence_finding: Access to AI raised confidence by 11.7 percentage points (77.0% vs 65.3%; Hedges' g = 0.54 [0.32, 0.77]) DESPITE approximately half of the AI's answers being faulty. And within the AI-Assisted condition, confidence did NOT decline as the number of faulty trials increased (p = 0.202). People met more wrong answers and did not get less sure.
what_it_actually_says.study_2: N = 485 (lab 138, Prolific 347). All had AI access except one randomly placed Brain-Only probe trial. Time Pressure n = 228 (30-second countdown) vs Control n = 257. Time pressure lowered accuracy everywhere but did not change the selectivity of following accurate vs faulty advice (interaction p = 0.102). Brain-Only probe: 32.6% under time pressure vs 46.9% control.
what_it_actually_says.study_3: N = 450, Prolific. Incentives + Feedback n = 238 ($0.20 per correct answer, a $20 lottery entry, and immediate item-level correct/incorrect feedback) vs Control n = 212. It WORKED, partially: override of faulty advice more than doubled, 20.0% to 42.3%. But surrender persisted — the accuracy gap between accurate and faulty trials was still about 44 points under incentives against about 50 under control.
what_it_actually_says.the_synthesis: Preregistered trial-level synthesis, N = 1,372, 9,593 trials. Correct responding over 16 times greater when the AI was correct (OR = 16.07 [11.50, 22.46]). Cohen's h by study 0.83 / 0.86 / 0.78; trial-weighted 0.82.
what_it_actually_says.the_number_to_quote: On trials where the AI was engaged AND WRONG: 73.2% cognitive surrender (followed it), 19.7% cognitive offloading (overrode it and got the answer right), 7.1% failed overrides (resisted it and were still wrong). Incentives and feedback moved surrender down to 57.9%; time pressure cut offloading to 6.2%.
what_it_actually_says.individual_differences: Trust in AI predicted more surrender over offloading (OR = 4.36 [2.95, 6.46]). Need for Cognition (OR = 0.46) and fluid intelligence (OR = 0.37) predicted resistance. In Study 2, AI-Users and Independents did NOT differ in fluid IQ — the split is disposition, not ability.
limitations_verbatim_substance: Controlled experimental environments: high internal validity, 'may limit generalizability to real-world settings'. They call for field experiments.
The CRT 'captures a specific form of cognition'; they call for probabilistic reasoning, everyday decision-making and moral judgment.

THE ONE THAT MATTERS FOR US: 'the current studies provide a snapshot of decision-making under a single set of exposures to System 3.' They explicitly call for longitudinal or adaptive paradigms and ask 'Does trust in System 3 grow or attenuate with experience? How do people learn to detect or correct faulty AI outputs over time?' They are not claiming the durable effect. Nobody in this literature is.
Other moderators and individual differences unexamined — cognitive load, accountability, age, gender, personality, neurotypicality, technological ability.
what_it_actually_says.arithmetic_check: 359 + 485 + 450 = 1,294, against a synthesis N of 1,372. Footnote 1 explains it: the ancillary Study 1 online sample was included in the synthesis. 1,294 + 81 = 1,375, three more than reported — presumably exclusions, detailed in Web Appendix C, which we have not read. what_it_actually_says.the_framing_question: Tri-System Theory is a wrapper. The empirical results stand without it: people consulted the assistant, followed it four times in five even when it was wrong, and got more confident while doing so. The piece should report the experiments and mention the framing, not lead with System 3.

what_it_actually_says.CORRECTION_TO_OUR_CLAIM:
We called this 'the mirror image of Gerlich — the same design weakness pointed the other way'. That is unfair and now corrected. Gerlich measured both variables in ONE instrument at ONE sitting. what_it_actually_says.design: Retrospective observational, four Polish endoscopy centres which implemented AI polyp detection at the end of 2021. After implementation, colonoscopies were conducted with or without AI according to the date of examination. Three months before against three months after, September 2021 to March 2022. Primary outcome: ADR of standard, NON-AI-assisted colonoscopy. Multivariable logistic regression for independent factors.
what_it_actually_says.who: 19 endoscopists — 16 physicians, 3 surgeons — each with more than 2,000 colonoscopies, averaging 27.6 years since graduation, range 8 to 39.
what_it_actually_says.result: 1,443 standard non-AI colonoscopies, 795 before and 648 after. Mean patient age 58, 59% female. ADR fell from 28.4% (226/795) to 22.4% (145/648): -6.0 percentage points, 95% CI -10.5 to -1.6. In the regression, the independent factors lowering ADR were patient female sex, age under 60, operator specialty (surgeons vs physicians), and exposure to AI.
what_it_actually_says.THE_CONFOUNDER_THAT_MATTERS_MOST: Their eighth limitation, and the one the secondary appraisal missed entirely. Procedures nearly DOUBLED after implementation — 795 before against 1,382 after (734 with AI, 648 without) — across equal three-month windows, because Poland suspended its colonoscopy-based colorectal cancer screening programme on 1 January 2022. That freed capacity and the centres drew patients off the waiting list. The population being scoped in the second period was plausibly different from the first, and the authors say so.
what_it_actually_says.other_limitations_they_state: Cohorts may not be comparable on indication and procedural context (mitigated by regression); only one AI system; only 19 experienced endoscopists, so generalisability to trainees is unknown and they call for that work; too few procedures per endoscopist for a reliable endoscopist-level analysis, treated as a subgroup with cautious interpretation; a possible time effect, mitigated by the short window and the operators' long experience; NO BLINDING, which 'may introduce unforeseen biases'; NO WITHDRAWAL TIME DATA and no sample size calculation; sessile serrated lesions excluded from ADR, which a recent Dutch study links to post-colonoscopy cancer; the first 100 colonoscopies per centre excluded for familiarisation, with uneven per-endoscopist exposure inside that; and low examination counts for some endoscopists.
what_it_actually_says.their_causal_language: 'Continuous exposure to AI MAY reduce ADR of standard, non-AI assisted colonoscopy, suggesting a negative impact on endoscopist BEHAVIOUR.'
what_it_actually_says.their_own_call: 'We emphasize the urgent need for robust prospective studies such as randomized crossover trials to assess its generalizability and call for more behavioral research to understand the currently under-investigated mechanisms of how AI affects physician capability.'
what_it_actually_says.PEER_REVIEW_VISIBLY_DID_ITS_JOB: The SSRN preprint of 26 December 2024 concluded: 'Continuous exposure to AI REDUCED ADR... suggesting a negative impact on endoscopist PERFORMANCE.' The accepted version says 'MAY reduce... a negative impact on endoscopist BEHAVIOUR.' The hedge was added and the noun changed. That is worth printing: in a literature where almost nothing is peer reviewed, here is a case where review made a claim more careful, and the softening is visible in the record.
what_it_actually_says.what_the_piece_must_carry_alongside_the_: The screening-programme suspension, the absence of withdrawal-time data, the absence of blinding, the 19 operators, and the authors' own 'may'. A headline that says AI is deskilling doctors drops all five.

the_six_key_studies: Wang et al. (2023), JAMIA — randomised crossover, 40 clinicians, ACL tears on MRI. AI raised accuracy 87.2% to 96.4%, AND 45.5% of the errors made under AI were attributable to automation bias. An 'AI suppression' strategy — withholding outputs with high misleading probability — cut automation bias by 41.7%.

Savardi et al. (2025), Insights Imaging — 32 radiology residents, COVID-19 chest X-rays. Sensitivity up 12% (0.73 to 0.85), reading time down 18% (68s to 56s), and PERFORMANCE STABLE AT THREE MONTHS with specificity maintained around 0.80. A NULL for deskilling, and it must be in the piece.
Tschandl et al. (2020), Lancet Digital Health — dermatology. AI improved accuracy but induced automation bias.
Ainechi et al. (2022), Endoscopy — polyp detection. AI raised adenoma detection and reduced variability between endoscopists; the flagged risk is reduced training in visual recognition.
Bellahsen-Harrar et al. (2025), Mod Pathol — 28 pathologists under time pressure abandoned 7% of initially CORRECT judgments when shown erroneous AI suggestions, and error severity increased.
Rebolj et al. (2022), Cytopathology — structural, not cognitive: England's move to HPV primary screening cut cytology workload 80-85% and laboratories from 45 to 8. Fewer cases to learn on.

THE_PROBLEM_WITH_IT._why_this_matters: This is the review a doctor or a policymaker would read to find out what the deskilling evidence says. Reading it against the two underlying papers we had already read at source, it misdescribes both.
THE_PROBLEM_WITH_IT.one_it_calls_the_colonoscopy_study_a_ran: Its ABSTRACT says: 'In a multicenter randomized trial in colonoscopy, the adenoma detection rate (ADR) dropped significantly from 28.4% to 22.4%...'. Budzyn et al. is a RETROSPECTIVE OBSERVATIONAL STUDY — it says so in its own title and its authors list eleven limitations flowing from that design. The review's body does say 'multicenter observational study'; the abstract, which is what most people read, says randomized trial. The single strongest claim in the deskilling literature is promoted one level of evidence in the abstract of the review that synthesises it.
THE_PROBLEM_WITH_IT.two_the_mammography_citation_does_not_ma:
The Radiology section says: 'a controlled reader study published in 2023 evaluated 27 radiologists interpreting 720 mammograms with and without AI support. When AI provided incorrect recommendations, radiologists' error rates increased by 12%-15%, even among experienced readers', citing reference 16. Reference 16 is GOMMERS ET AL., Radiology 2025;316(1):e243688 — 12 radiologists, 150 mammograms, published 2025, and it found AI IMPROVED accuracy from AUC 0.93 to 0.97. We read Gommers directly tonight; the description matches almost nothing about it.

What the description DOES match, on every checkable particular but one, is DRATSCH ET AL. (2023), 'Automation Bias in Mammography: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence BI-RADS Suggestions on Reader Performance', Radiology 307(4) e222176 — 27 radiologists, 2023, incorrect AI BI-RADS suggestions. Dratsch does not appear anywhere in the review's reference list. The mammogram count does not match either paper: Dratsch used 50 cases, of which 49 were analysed, not 720.
THE_PROBLEM_WITH_IT.three_and_it_understates_the_effect_it_d: 'Error rates increased by 12%-15%' badly undersells Dratsch. When the AI gave an incorrect BI-RADS suggestion, readers were correct 19.8% (inexperienced), 24.8% (moderately experienced) and 45.5% (very experienced) of the time. That is accuracy collapsing, not error rates edging up.
THE_PROBLEM_WITH_IT.FAIRNESS: These are errors of citation and characterisation in a review whose substance — that the evidence is scarce, fragmented and consistent in direction — we have no reason to doubt and which we are relying on. The review is open access, declares no funding and no conflicts, and states plainly that it used Copilot for proofreading. Its conclusion is measured. The piece reports the mismatches because they matter to a reader deciding how much weight the deskilling literature bears, not to discredit the authors.
TO_VERIFY_BEFORE_PRINTING: Read Dratsch et al. at source rather than through a repository PDF summary — DONE for the headline figures, but confirm the case count and the three accuracy figures against the paper itself.
Confirm reference 16 in the published version, in case the online version differs from the PDF the operator supplied.
Check whether the review has a correction notice.

sources.FOURTH_PROBLEM_THE_PRISMA_FLOW: Read off Figure 1 directly on 2026-08-30, after the source advocate asked whether the numbers we quote are the numbers the paper prints. what_it_actually_says.design: NOT LIVE COLONOSCOPY. 21 participants — 10 novice (6 physicians, 4 nurses) and 11 experienced (7 physicians, 4 nurses) — watched 29 recorded colonoscopy video sequences while wearing eye-tracking glasses, pressing a button on detecting a polyp. Crossover design, two assessments with a THREE-WEEK WASHOUT, each participant seeing every video once with and once without CADe overlay. 1,218 experiments. The CADe system was GI Genius (Medtronic), March 2020 version, run without audio cues. 17 videos contained a single polyp; the other 12 contained only false-positive activations, graded mild (<1s), moderate (1-3s) and severe (>3s). Eye-tracking data were analysable for 17 of the 21 — four were excluded because prescription glasses interfered with the device.
what_it_actually_says.reaction_time: The CADe system's own first detection time was a median 1.16s (99%CI 0.40-3.43) against participants' 2.97s (2.53-3.77). But participants USING CADe were at 2.90s (2.55-3.38) — statistically indistinguishable from working without it. The machine was faster; the people were not.
what_it_actually_says.THE_EYE_TRAVEL_NUMBERS:
Table 1, median eye travel distance in cm, 99% CI. All participants, all videos: 248.86 (221.39-282.88) without CADe against 232.68 (210.43-262.33) with, P<0.001. Experienced: 247.89 against 227.09. Novice: 255.66 against 247.89. False-positive-only videos: 368.95 against 329.76.

THE EFFECT IS REAL AND MODEST — about 6.5% overall, and only about 3% in novices. The piece prints the numbers, not the word 'reduced'.
what_it_actually_says.misinterpretation_got_WORSE: Participants falsely identified a polyp in a median of 4 cases (99%CI 2-5) without CADe and 6 cases (4-7) WITH it, P=0.001. Both novices and experienced participants misread normal mucosa more often with the AI. That is mis-skilling in Ke et al.'s sense, measured.
what_it_actually_says.they_barely_looked_at_the_boxes: Participants inspected the false-positive bounding boxes for less than half the time the boxes were on screen — 43.79% overall (95%CI 40.71-54.89), novices 49.50%, experienced 42.68%, and lowest of all for the briefest activations.
what_it_actually_says.their_own_interpretation_verbatim: 'Effort, as expressed by eye travel distance, decreased, and gaze remained more focused, presumably waiting for a bounding box to appear. This might be efficient but risks missing a polyp that is not captured by the system.'
what_it_actually_says.the_learning_curve_sentence: 'Extrapolating this finding raises the concern that CADe systems may have an impact on the learning curve of colonoscopy trainees by preventing them from developing the visual "bottom U" pattern of high-performing endoscopists.' The bottom-U pattern comes from Lami et al., Endoscopy 2018.
what_it_actually_says.the_deskilling_sentence_verbatim: Abstract: 'Possible consequences of these findings might be prolonged examination time and deskilling.' Conclusion: '...suggests a potential risk of overreliance and deskilling when these systems are used.' NOTE THE HEDGING — 'possible', 'might', 'potential risk'. They are careful and the piece is careful with them.
what_it_actually_says.their_stated_limitation: 'Limitations of the study include the experimental design using only short video sequences that were chosen in order to increase the number of voluntary participants.' Twenty-one people watching clips is not twenty-one people doing colonoscopies.

sources.how_the_piece_uses_it: As the MECHANISM, credited to Troya and colleagues and to Zhou for proposing it — with its own limits stated in the same breath: a video study of 21 people, a 6.5% change in eye travel, and authors who wrote 'possible' and 'might'. sources.title: Pedersen TA, Mori Y, Botteri E, Engjom T, Seip B, Dimcevski GG, Havre RF (2026) — Learning and deskilling effects of artificial intelligence in colonoscopy among endoscopists with different levels of experience: a pragmatic, prospective trial. Endoscopy 2026;58:1003–1014, published online 3 June 2026.
sources.used_for: THE NULL RESULT. Three successive phases — before CADe, during CADe, after CADe removal — with the same endoscopists throughout. 13 endoscopists (7 inexperienced, 6 experienced), 5,013 colonoscopies. Primary endpoint PDR-5, the proportion of colonoscopies detecting at least one polyp 5 mm or larger. Inexperienced: 31.9% (216/678) to 39.5% (257/651) with CADe, OR 1.43, 95% CI 1.11–1.84; phase 1 to phase 3, 31.9% (216/678) to 36.3% (173/476), OR 1.03, 95% CI 0.79–1.34. No significant effect among the experienced between any phases.
sources.why_it_matters: It falsifies the sentence this page carried: 'So the honest position on a null result is that we do not have one.' It also has the design the page says the field needs — the same operators watched before, during and after withdrawal, rather than two periods compared after the fact. It is not randomised and its endpoint is polyp detection at 5 mm, not adenoma detection, so it does not settle the question; but it is prospective, multicentre, larger than the Polish study in procedures, and it points the other way.

VERBATIM.conclusion: Conclusions: PDR-5 of inexperienced endoscopists increased when CADe was used. In non-CADe-assisted colonoscopy, no upskilling or deskilling was observed following a period of CADe exposure.
VERBATIM.design: Methods: We performed a prospective, multicenter, registry-based, pragmatic clinical trial. The primary end point was change in the proportion of colonoscopies with detection of at least one polyp >=5 mm (PDR-5). Each endoscopist performed colonoscopies in three successive phases: 1) before CADe exposure, 2) during CADe use, and 3) after CADe removal.
VERBATIM.results: Results: 13 endoscopists (7 inexperienced, 6 experienced) performed 5013 colonoscopies; median patient age was 59 years (interquartile range 44-71) and 2703 (53.9%) were women. ... CADe temporarily increased PDR-5 among inexperienced endoscopists from phase 1 to 2 (31.9% [216/678] to 39.5% [257/651]; odds ratio [OR] 1.43, 95%CI 1.11-1.84). There was no significant change between phases 1 and 3 (31.9% [216/678] to 36.3% [173/476]; OR 1.03, 95%CI 0.79-1.34). There was no significant CADe effect on PDR-5 among experienced endoscopists between phases.
VERBATIM.THE_RECONCILIATION_WITH_BUDZYN: The finding of no significant effects of CADe on learning or deskilling among experienced endoscopists differs from the recent study by Budzyn et al., which found a significant deskilling effect among experienced endoscopists while they were exposed to CADe. A study by Troya et al. showed decreased eye travel distance when using CADe, which could explain why such deskilling happened in the study by Budzyn et al. However, there is a distinct difference in study design between our study and the Budzyn study. We evaluated the effect of exposure to CADe “after” CADe was removed, whereas Budzyn et al. investigated how endoscopists perform non-CADe-assisted colonoscopy “while” they were exposed to CADe in the other colonoscopies they performed during the same time period. Thus, it is considered that the effect of exposure to CADe will be stronger in the Budzyn study than in our study, suggesting that the deskilling effect may be a temporal phenomenon that disappears over time after CADe is removed.
VERBATIM.their_narrowed_conclusion: Additionally, the absence of an observable post-exposure reduction in PDR-5 compared with pre-exposure argues against the idea that exposure to CADe erodes skills, at least for nonexperienced endoscopists, although such skill reduction has been observed in another study involving only experienced endoscopists [10]. — reference 10 is Budzyn et al.
VERBATIM.their_most_important_limitation: There are several limitations to this study. The most important is the use of PDR-5 as a quality indicator for lesion detection, rather than the gold standard ADR. ... We acknowledge that this quality indicator is less well-validated than ADR.
VERBATIM.the_time_effect: it is challenging to draw such a conclusion based solely on the change in PDR-5 between phases 1 and 3, given that there is always a time effect in which endoscopists may naturally upskill or deskill over time. Mean inclusion time from the first colonoscopy among the inexperienced group was 6.8 months in phase 1, 17.7 months in phase 2, and 23.8 months in phase 3. Such long-term exposure to a medical procedure may play a role in skill development, which needs to be considered in analysis of upskilling and deskilling.
VERBATIM.other_limitations: A possible limitation of the multivariable analyses is the risk of underpowering. We might have overlooked otherwise significant differences due to limited sample size. In particular, the inexperienced endoscopists had differences in the case-mix between phases 1 and 3, with higher age, more women, more symptoms, and fewer IBD patients in phase 3. This difference in case-mix may have influenced the PDR-5. ... the definition of an experienced endoscopist is not well established in the literature. Finally, we used only one type of AI device.
VERBATIM.why_the_experienced_group_may_show_nothi: The experienced endoscopists may also be less enthusiastic about a software tool intended to improve their performance, leading to an aversion to using it effectively. ... two endoscopists reported having CADe active throughout the entire examination (including intubation of the colon), while the remaining endoscopists activated CADe on withdrawal from the cecum.
VERBATIM.endoscopist_level_split: Looking at the endoscopist-level analysis among the inexperienced endoscopists, three deskilled, two unchanged, and two upskilled between phases 1 and 3. Among the experienced group, three deskilled and three upskilled.
VERBATIM.setting: pragmatic clinical trial from November 2021 to June 2025 ... 5013 patients, 3 centers, Norway. The 13 endoscopists comprised 12 physicians and 1 surgeon. Inexperienced mean age 41.1 years, experienced 50.7 years. Median withdrawal time across all phases 10 minutes (IQR 8-16) inexperienced, 9 minutes (IQR 7-11) experienced.

sources.WHAT_THE_ABSTRACT_DID_NOT_SAY: Four things, and each of them changed the page. (1) The authors reconcile their result with Budzyn themselves, on a design difference — during exposure versus after withdrawal — that no coverage of either study has reported, and they propose that deskilling may be temporary. (2) They cite Troya as the mechanism for Budzyn, which is the link this page makes independently. (3) They narrow their own conclusion to nonexperienced endoscopists and explicitly leave Budzyn's finding in experienced endoscopists standing. (4) They give the limitations that matter: PDR-5 rather than ADR as 'the most important', a three-and-a-half-year time effect, a case-mix shift between phases, possible underpowering, and one device. THE PAGE HAD SAID the prospective study found nothing 'most clearly in its experienced group'. That was wrong in emphasis and has been removed: the experienced group shows no effect in EITHER direction, including no benefit while the tool ran, which the authors attribute partly to algorithm aversion. A group that did not visibly gain from a tool is weak evidence about what losing it does. Reading the abstract and writing four paragraphs from it was the same error this repository already has a rule against: a review is a hop, not a source, and so is an abstract.

crossing_observation._the_finding: The single best real-world study of skill degradation from AI use sits in gastroenterology, and the AI-and-thinking conversation has not picked it up.
crossing_observation.checked: Of the four general-audience pieces in this ledger — Forbes (S in premise carriers), EDUCAUSE Review (S014), Goldin (S013) and The Conversation (S012) — NONE cites Budzyń et al. EDUCAUSE cites the MIT preprint, Singh et al., Lee et al. and Dergaa et al.; Goldin cites the MIT preprint, the 758-consultant study, a Scientific Reports tutor study and an October 2025 guided-versus-unguided experiment; The Conversation cites one crutch-effect study; the Forbes piece cites nothing at all.
crossing_observation.HOW_FAR_THIS_CAN_BE_STATED: As written: 'none of the four pieces we examined cites it'. NOT as 'nobody has connected them', which is an unbounded universal over everything published and belongs to the counterexample hunter, not to us. The claim to be attacked before drafting is: 'No general-audience account of AI and thinking has brought the colonoscopy deskilling result into the same frame as the essay-writing and reasoning studies.'
crossing_observation.why_it_would_be_the_contribution: It is the only place in this literature where the question is asked about a real skill, in real work, with a real consequence, over months — and it is in a journal the people arguing about ChatGPT and essays have no reason to read. Carrying it across is translation, which is what this publication is for.
crossing_observation.NARROWED_2026_08_29:
The claim as first written — that the AI-and-thinking conversation has not picked the colonoscopy result up — is TOO STRONG. Fortune carried it on 26 August 2025 to a general business readership and connected it to the Microsoft/CMU judgment-atrophy work and to Air France 447. STAT carried it to a professional audience. The crossing has happened.

WHAT HAS NOT HAPPENED, and this is the third narrowing of a novelty claim today: nobody has set it beside the essay-writing and reasoning studies AND been honest about what it does and does not show. Fortune printed the result with none of the eleven limitations its own authors list. The contribution is not the crossing. It is the crossing done carefully — which is the whole premise of this publication and a smaller, truer claim than the one we had an hour ago.

THE_EXTRACT_RULE.rule: A source whose access state is human_read, or any source this page takes a FIGURE or a QUOTATION from, must carry the sentences that figure or quotation comes from, VERBATIM, in this file. Not a summary of them. Not a page range. The sentences.
THE_EXTRACT_RULE.why: The operator supplied the Shaw & Nave PDF on 2026-08-29 and it was read. S017 recorded the page ranges read and what the study means, but not the sentence carrying the 11.7 confidence figure. When the page gate questioned that figure on 2026-08-30 the record could not answer, and the operator had to be sent back to a document he had already provided. He was right to be surprised. A conversation is not storage: it is compacted, and an attachment's text goes with it. This file is storage. What is not written down here did not survive.
THE_EXTRACT_RULE.the_second_half_of_the_lesson: The PDFs were still on disk in the session's own upload directory the whole time. The search that concluded they were gone looked in the working directory and the mounted folders and did not look there, and the conclusion was reported to the operator as fact. Not finding something is a statement about where you looked.

THE_MISS.what: Pedersen et al. was published online on 3 June 2026 — in Endoscopy, in the same specialty, on the same question, with the senior author of our central study as a co-author — and this page was drafted on 30 August 2026 saying no null result existed. Two fact-check gate runs, a source advocate pass, five counterexample hunts and a lint pass all went over the page without finding it. An outside reviewer found it in one sitting.
THE_MISS.why_it_survived: Not because it was hidden. Because the search that would have found it was recorded as NOT RUN and the piece was written anyway. The watch entry for 2026-08-30 lists under not_checked: 'W1 — no registry search run' and 'W2 — no citation sweep run'. The machinery correctly reported that it had not looked; nothing stopped the draft proceeding past that report. An unrun check is not a pass — the rule was already written, and it was applied to the gate's findings and not to our own.
THE_MISS.the_fix_this_argues_for: preflight should block a draft whose own watch file records an unrun check on a question that would change the piece. The watch module already knows which questions are open and when each was last checked; nothing consults it before a draft is gated. That is a code change, not a resolution.

THE_CITATION_COUNT.what_happened: The retracted meta-analysis's citation count was printed three ways in one day. The page said 'more than 500'. A gate run VERIFIED 500+. The next run said 266. Nature's own article page read 402 at about 17:00 and 399 an hour later. Independent reports give 262, 266 and 270 depending on whether they count the journal's own counter, Springer Nature journals only, or everything.
THE_CITATION_COUNT.the_rule: A live metric is not a fact and should not be printed as one, however carefully it is dated. It moves while you look at it, and a reader who checks will find a different number and conclude we were careless. Page and email now say 'several hundred', which is true on every count and will stay true.
